reconcile.connective: Matthew Henry treats the disciples' baptizing as Jesus's own act, done by his orders and in his name.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible catalogs this exact pairing, posing John 3:22's claim that Jesus baptized against John 4:2's flat denial as a direct factual clash.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/baptize.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: He himself baptized not, with his own hand, but his disciples by his orders and directions, as appears, Joh 4:2. But his disciples' baptizing was his baptizing.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Henry directly reconciles the two verses by treating the disciples' baptizing, done under Jesus's orders, as Jesus's own baptizing -- the standard agency harmonization for John 3:22 vs 4:2.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-1714)
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry's own note on John 3:22 treats this exact tension directly, citing John 4:2 and resolving it via agency ('his disciples' baptizing was his baptizing'). John Haley's Alleged Discrepancies (1874) was checked (full-text search of the archive.org djvu.txt for 'baptiz', 'John iii. 22', 'John iv. 2') and its only 'Baptism' entry treats a different pairing (Matt 28:19 vs 1 Cor 1:14-17, Paul's non-baptizing), not John 3:22/4:2, so the row's own harmonizing commentator is used instead.
